subject: mathematics
question_text: For what values of x in the first quadrant is (2 tan x)/(1 − tan²x) positive?

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 8 TRIGONOMETRIC RATIOS, Very Short Answer question 21, book p.86. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split rewards recognising the expression as tan 2x first — with the point x = π/4 where it has no value named there — and the sign interval second, because the answer is a set and a bare inequality without the excluded point is incomplete. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern; Trigonometric Ratios and Transformations holds two of those ten slots. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Checked numerically: (2 tan x)/(1 − tan²x) equals tan 2x to ten decimal places at x = 1°, 30°, 44.9°, 45.1°, 60° and 89°; it is positive at 1° and 30°, negative at 60° and 89°, and at x = 45° the denominator is 0 so the expression has no value. Reading of the stem: 'in the first quadrant' is taken as the open interval 0 < x < π/2, which is why x = 0 is not in the answer — at x = 0 the value is 0, and 0 is not positive.

recall_prompt: Say what this expression really is, and say which values of x in the first quadrant make it positive.

steps.label: Recognise the tan 2x form
steps.margin_note: First mark. The expression is the tan 2x formula. It has no value where 1 − tan²x = 0, and in the first quadrant that is x = π/4, so that point must be named.
steps.memory_tip: 2t/(1 − t²) with t = tan x is the tan 2x formula. It fails only where 1 − tan²x = 0, that is at x = π/4.

steps.label: Find where tan 2x is positive
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Doubling sends 0 < x < π/2 onto 0 < 2x < π. Tangent is positive on the first half of that and negative on the second, so the answer is the open interval (0, π/4).
steps.memory_tip: Doubling turns 0 < x < π/2 into 0 < 2x < π. Tangent is positive on the first half only, so x < π/4.

steps.why: Doubling x sends the open first quadrant (0, π/2) onto (0, π). Tangent is positive on the first half of that range and negative on the second, so only x < π/4 survives. At x = 0 the value is 0, which is not positive, so 0 is not in the set either.
common_mistakes: Giving the whole first quadrant as the answer.
Including x = π/4, where the expression has no value.
Writing 0 ≤ x, although the value at x = 0 is 0 and 0 is not positive.
